quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns. Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to support your body weight.

questions.question: The human body removes alcohol at a rate of:

options.text: About one drink per hour.
About two drinks per hour.
About three drinks per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. This varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake. Separating these actions keeps you in control.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to veer out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Which lane position is usually best for keeping other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in beside you. This also makes you more visible in a car's rearview mirror.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad or trolley tracks while staying in your lane. Changing your path to cross tracks might push you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Severely limits your vision.
Allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It provides good side vision for safe riding.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be below their ankles.
Cover their ankles.
Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover their ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the part of your lane farthest from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther away from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it invites the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it invites the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the farthest part of your lane when being passed. This may signal the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What can a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face during a crash. It also protects you from everyday hazards like rocks from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see the road better.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Visibility is lower at night, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: What should you wear to reduce the chance of serious injury in a crash?

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Skip the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, stop at the stop line first. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the crossroad. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Make sure your front wheel does not enter the crossroad while you are looking.

questions.question: What does it feel like when your front tire goes flat?

options.text: Heavy steering.
Loose steering.
Soft steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy steering.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This reduces your reaction time if you need to stop.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves, as they could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to stay away from other traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves, as they could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both the front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should they do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: Is hearing protection important for motorcycle riders?

options.text: It is not recommended.
It is recommended only for long rides.
It is recommended for every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is recommended for every ride.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection on every ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position increases visibility, helps you avoid hazards and blind spots, discourages other drivers from entering your lane, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: In areas with potential danger, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Keep their current speed.
Assume they are safe.
Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shops, schools, or construction zones, reduce speed and cover the clutch and brake levers to react quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: Is a plastic face shield required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, it is required by law.
No, but it is recommended.
No, it is not encouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, but it is recommended.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield is not required, but riders are encouraged to wear one to protect their face and eyes. Full face shields offer the best protection.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers are required by law to wear a helmet on motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, and motorized bicycles.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can become dirty and block the view.
Mirrors are always unreliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Relying only on mirrors is not enough to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle becomes stuck, immediately use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch to remove power from the rear wheel until you can safely stop.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what does it mean if you cannot see the truck's mirrors?

options.text: The driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Avoid staying in the truck's blind spots.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?

options.text: At intersections.
On open roads.
In parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car collisions happen at intersections. The most common cause is when a driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
